root.claim: There is one deterministic Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes that, for every $n\ge1$, returns the exact $2n$-bit product of two $n$-bit integers in worst-case time $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ with $\kappa=2^{-182}$, so the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture fails in this model.
root.method: Follow the Harvey–van der Hoeven reduction of the radix-digit convolution to power-of-two transforms over $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ (Chinese-remainder axes, Gaussian resampling, chirps, a coefficient twist, synthetic transforms), replace its two $\Theta(n\log n)$ bottlenecks, address rearrangement and butterfly layers, by two tape procedures that save a power of their width, recover the exact product by rounding and carries, and choose the parameters so that every cost is $O(n(\log n)^{1-\kappa})$.

motivation.text: In the synthetic-transform representation the whole transform is address rearrangements, signed shifts and two-point butterflies, and merely scanning $\Theta(n)$ bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$; so beating $n\log n$ needs savings in both data movement and arithmetic, which the two procedures supply inside an otherwise standard reduction.

quote.quote: Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of $\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$.

root.salient: A single fixed machine saves a strict power of the logarithm at every input length, so $T_A(n)/(n\lg n)\to0$ rather than merely having limit inferior zero, though the exponent $\kappa=2^{-182}$ is astronomically small.

motivation.text: A call at parameter $mf$ makes $s$ calls at parameter $f$ on streams of volume $V/W$, so after dividing cost by volume the recursive contribution grows by $s/W<m$ per factor $m$ of the parameter instead of by $m$; iterating this strict inequality yields a power saving in the width.

quote.quote: This strict inequality is the source of the power saving.

quote.quote: costs $O(V)$ if the offset can be prepared in $b^{O(1)}$ time from the fixed number of control values.

children.claim: There are two fixed linear networks, an XOR network over $\mathbb F_2$ with $W_{\rm b}$ wires and a $\mathbb Z[i,1/2]$ network with $W_{\rm c}$ wires, that exchange two banks of $N$ values with prescribed signs and restore every scratch wire, and whose frame changes need $s_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m$ and $s_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m$ smaller calls, indeed $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$ and $s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c}<m^\sigma$ with $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$.
children.method: Fix one three-stage scalar exchange schedule, attach nested nondegenerate subspaces of an $m$-dimensional bilinear space to its vertices as labels so that each edge costs its label-dimension change, count those changes, and realize the labels as rational projections (bit network) or binary phase frames (complex network).

motivation.text: The common-frame identity shows that only the endpoint frames affect what each role receives, so the intermediate frames are free; choosing them from nested labels makes each edge's cost a dimension change, and the saving becomes a counting statement about labels.

quote.quote: Once the scalar routing is fixed, the endpoint frames determine the array operator on each route; the intermediate frames can then be chosen to make each edge change inexpensive.

children.claim: Along all edges of either network the label dimensions change by a total of exactly $Wm-2N+2L$, where the lost dimension $L=Ich$ comes only from the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4, and $L/N$ equals $100/539$ or $101/539$, below $1/2$.
children.method: Build the exchange schedule and the frame invariant, attach nested labels to every vertex, telescope the signed dimension changes through the gates down to the terminal dimensions, and add back twice the loss on the only decreasing edges.

motivation.text: Every gate has one common label on all its incidences, so signed changes cancel at gates and leave the sink total minus the source total, $Wm-2N$; only decreasing edges make the absolute total larger, and keeping their loss $L$ below $N/2$ keeps the total below $Wm$ even after the bit interface adds $N$ more.

quote.quote: The saving will come from keeping the total dimension lost on decreasing edges small relative to $N$.

children.salient: The deficit is minute (relative deficits of about $1.5\times10^{-11}$ and $3.7\times10^{-12}$ of $Wm$), yet any strict deficit compounds through the recursion into a power saving.

children.claim: For arbitrary initial scratch values, one forward invocation changes $y_S$ to $y_S+x_S$ and nothing else, and forward, inverse and forward invocations at the three stages send $(X_a,Y_a)\mapsto(-Y_a,X_a)$ for every $a$ while restoring every auxiliary wire, which over $\mathbb F_2$ is the plain swap of the two banks.
children.method: Subtract the old scratch contributions, copy and gather the sources into scratch, scatter and side-inject into the targets, then undo gather and copy; choose the side injection to cancel the central coefficients between distinct triples; compose three bank additions into a signed swap.

motivation.text: Scratch wires will later carry whole rows of the array with arbitrary contents, so the network must be correct for every initial scratch value; the transparent-computation pattern (subtract, compute, add, undo) makes the net effect independent of them, and three bank additions make the swap.

quote.quote: The scalar network allows these role values to be arbitrary, so the split supplies its scratch roles from existing rows.

children.claim: Rows 0–1 subtract $\mathcal Ja+\mathcal Rc$, rows 2–5 add $\mathcal R(c+\mathcal Gx)+\mathcal J(a+\mathcal Vx)$ and rows 6–7 restore the scratch vectors, so the net change of the targets is $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$ whatever the scratch values $a,c$.

quote.quote: The net target change is $(\mathcal J\mathcal V+\mathcal R\mathcal G)x$, independently of $a,c$.

children.claim: The central coefficient from $x_T$ to $y_S$ is $|S\cap T|\bmod2$ in the bit network, where side injection cancels exactly the intersection-one neighbors, and $(|S\cap T|-1)/2$ in the complex network, where it cancels intersections zero and two; the self coefficient is $1$, so both net maps are $y\gets y+x$.

quote.quote: Thus both net maps are $y\gets y+x$.

children.claim: The inverse schedule gives $X\gets X-Y$, so the three stages take $(x,y)$ to $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$, each invocation restoring its own scratch wires.

quote.quote: Starting from $(x,y)$, the three stages give $(x,y+x)$, then $(-y,y+x)$, then $(-y,x)$.

children.claim: If each source, gate and sink $v$ carries an invertible frame $D_v$ on the arrays and each edge from $u$ to $v$ applies $D_vD_u^{-1}$, the array network implements $D_{\rm out}\mathsf S_\Omega D_{\rm in}^{-1}$, so a role routed from $w$ to $\rho(w)$ with sign $\varepsilon_w$ receives $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ whatever the intermediate frames are.
children.method: Carry the invariant 'the stored array is the vertex frame applied to the logical array' from the sources, where it holds by definition, across edges and through gates to the sinks.

motivation.text: A frame mixes addresses inside one wire's array, while a gate combines wires at one fixed address, so by linearity a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate; this frees the intermediate frames, and each edge then pays only for changing its frame.

quote.quote: When the values are replaced by arrays, a common representation on all wires at a gate lets that gate act pointwise without disturbing the representation.

children.claim: At a gate all incidences share the frame $D_v$, and $\sum_jc_jD_v\varphi_j=D_v(\sum_jc_j\varphi_j)$ by linearity, so the invariant survives every gate as well as every edge.

quote.quote: Thus the common frame commutes with the pointwise gate, and the invariant continues to the sinks.

children.claim: For a signed role permutation the route from $w$ applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$, on the auxiliary roles as well as on the data roles.

quote.quote: All roles, including the auxiliary roles, enter this identity.

children.claim: Labels built from tensor products of triple indicators $t_T$, paired by the rational form $I-J/9$ (so $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$) in the bit network and by the dot product over $\mathbb F_2$ in the complex network, can be attached to all vertices so that every edge joins nested nondegenerate labels, the labels run from $U_a$ on $X_a$ and $0$ elsewhere to $\mathcal F$ or $U_a^\perp$, and the only decreasing edges are the central-wire edges from time 3 to time 4, each losing dimension $h$.

motivation.text: The network's neighbor relation is defined by intersection sizes, and the pairings make neighboring triple lines orthogonal; that orthogonality is exactly what lets a side wire's label move from one triple's line into the other triple's orthogonal complement without losing dimension.

quote.quote: Orthogonality of the corresponding indicator vectors permits the subspace assignments.

adds.name: triple indicator
adds.meaning: The 0/1 indicator vector, in $\mathbb Q^h$ or $\mathbb F_2^h$, of a three-element subset $T$ of the ground set.

adds.name: ambient label space
adds.meaning: The tensor cube $F^{\otimes3}$, of dimension $m=h^3$, in which every label lies.

children.claim: Over $\mathbb Q$, $\langle t_S,t_T\rangle=|S\cap T|-1$ and $\langle t_T,t_T\rangle=2$, and over $\mathbb F_2$, $t_T\cdot t_T=1$, so every triple line is nondegenerate and neighboring triple lines are orthogonal in either label field.

quote.quote: Thus every triple line is nondegenerate, and neighboring triple lines are orthogonal, in the label field belonging to either construction.

quote.quote: A central wire returns once from the former label to the latter, losing exactly $P\otimes F$.

quote.quote: The side edge $2\to5$ uses the neighbor relation essentially.

children.claim: Each touched wire enters and leaves a gate with the same gate label, so the signed changes telescope to the sink total $Wm-N$ minus the source total $N$, that is $Wm-2N$.

quote.quote: The signed sum of dimension changes telescopes at every gate: each touched wire has one incoming and one outgoing incidence with the same gate label.

children.claim: There are $Ic$ decreasing edges, one per central wire, each losing $h$, so passing from signed to absolute changes adds $2L$ with $L=Ich$.

quote.quote: There are $Ic$ decreasing edges, each of loss $h$; replacing signed changes by absolute changes adds $2L$.

children.claim: With $I=3v^2$ invocations, $N=v^3$, $v=\binom{100}3=161700$ and $c=100$ or $101$ central wires per invocation, $L/N=300c/v$ is $100/539$ for the bit network and $101/539$ for the complex network, both below $1/2$.

quote.quote: In particular, both are smaller than $1/2$.

children.claim: Assigning to each gate or sink with label $U$ the rational projection $P_U$ onto $U$ along $U^\perp$, and $-P_{U_a}$ to each source $X_a$, makes the XOR network route each input $w$ to $\rho(w)$ with $M_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{source}(w)}=I_m$ on every role, while the rational ranks of all edge differences sum to $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}m$.
children.method: Read each edge's matrix difference as a difference of nested projections, whose rank is the label-dimension change, correct for the $N$ negative source projections, and evaluate the endpoint differences.

motivation.text: On tape the frame of a matrix $M$ will be the address shear $(H,D)\mapsto(H+MD,D)$, and such shears compose by adding matrices; so endpoint matrix differences are the shears each role receives, and an edge whose difference has rank $a$ will cost $a$ smaller interchanges.

quote.quote: the endpoint matrix difference on each routed role is exactly the shear applied to that role.

children.salient: Every role, including the scratch roles whose rows carry arbitrary data, receives exactly the same shear $H\gets H+D$.

children.claim: For nested nondegenerate labels $U\subset V$, $P_V-P_U$ is the identity on $V\cap U^\perp$ and zero on its orthogonal complement, so its rational rank is $\dim V-\dim U$, in either edge direction.

quote.quote: Its rank is $\dim V-\dim U$; reversing the edge negates the matrix without changing its rank.

children.claim: The only exceptions are the $N$ sources $X_a$: at stage 1 the first gate on $X_a$ has label exactly $U_a$, so that edge's matrix is $2P_{U_a}$, of rank one, where the dimension change was zero.

quote.quote: Its first edge matrix is therefore $2P_{U_a}$, of rational rank one, where the corresponding dimension change was zero.

children.claim: Adding these $N$ ranks to $W_{\rm b}m-2N+2L_{\rm b}$ gives $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-N+2L_{\rm b}$, short of $W_{\rm b}m$ by $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$.

quote.quote: Its deficit from $W_{\rm b}m$ is $N-2L_{\rm b}>0$.

children.claim: For $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$, and every other role has zero source matrix and identity sink matrix, so every role gets difference $I_m$.

quote.quote: For an input $X_a$ the endpoint difference is $P_{U_a^\perp}-(-P_{U_a})=I_m$.

children.claim: With phase frames $\mathcal C_U=H^{\otimes m}\operatorname{diag}_x(i^{\operatorname{wt}(P_Ux)\bmod4})H^{\otimes m}$ on the complex network, each edge's frame change is a product of one two-point kernel $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse per vector of an orthonormal basis of the edge residual, these kernels number $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}<W_{\rm c}m$, and after diagonal corrections every role, on any number of columns, receives $C^{\otimes m}$.
children.method: Use that Hamming weight is additive modulo 4 on orthogonal binary vectors to factor each edge's phase change over an orthonormal residual basis, conjugate each factor by Hadamard matrices into a translation kernel, then telescope the frames and repair the one exceptional route with sign conjugations.

motivation.text: Each kernel $aI+bX_v$ is a two-point operator of the same kind as the layer being built, so a frame change factored into such kernels is a set of smaller calls; weight additivity modulo 4 holds exactly when supports meet in an even set, which orthogonality of the residual basis guarantees.

quote.quote: The intermediate frames are chosen so that every edge can be implemented by smaller calls to the same procedure.

children.salient: The endpoint operator is the same $C^{\otimes m}$ on every role, scratch roles included, although the exchanged route $X_a\to Y_a$ first gets $C^{-1}$ on the $27$ coordinates in the support of $u_a$.

children.claim: Since $\operatorname{wt}(z+w)=\operatorname{wt}(z)+\operatorname{wt}(w)-2|\operatorname{supp}z\cap\operatorname{supp}w|$, orthogonal vectors have weights adding modulo 4, so for $V=U\perp E$ with orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$ of $E$, $q_V(x)-q_U(x)=\sum_{v\in\mathcal B}\operatorname{wt}(v)[v\cdot x]\pmod4$, negated on a decreasing edge.

quote.quote: If $z\cdot w=0$, the intersection cardinality is even, so weight is additive modulo four.

children.claim: Each $v$ has odd weight, so its factor is $i^{\varepsilon[v\cdot x]}=\frac{1+i^\varepsilon}2+\frac{1-i^\varepsilon}2(-1)^{v\cdot x}$ with $\varepsilon=\pm1$, and $H\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)H=X$ turns the character into the translation $X_v$, giving $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.

quote.quote: The displayed phase therefore becomes $aI+bX_v$ or its inverse.

children.claim: Every nonzero binary residual has an orthonormal basis, so the kernels number the residual dimensions, $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-2N+2L_{\rm c}$, a deficit of $2N-2L_{\rm c}>0$ below $W_{\rm c}m$.

quote.quote: The deficit is $2N-2L_{\rm c}>0$.

children.claim: Zero and full labels have frames $I$ and $C^{\otimes m}$; on the route $X_a\to Y_a$ the frame is $C^{-1}$ on the $27$ coordinates of $\operatorname{supp}(u_a)$ and $C$ elsewhere, and the signs $Z_{a,k}$ before and $i^{27k}Z_{a,k}$ after turn it into $C^{\otimes mk}$ by $C=iZC^{-1}Z$.

quote.quote: The operator on this pair is therefore $C^{\otimes mk}$ as well.

children.claim: Negating the physical $X$ outputs and returning output role $\rho(w)$ to role $w$ leaves $C^{\otimes m}$ on every role, including every scratch role.

quote.quote: Every role, including every scratch role, now has the required forward tensor product.

children.claim: The relative deficits $\eta_{\rm b}=339/22587335000000$ and $\eta_{\rm c}=73/19906842167500$ both exceed $20\cdot2^{-50}$, and $\log m<20$ gives $m^{1-2^{-50}}>m(1-\eta)$, so $s_{\rm b}/W_{\rm b}<m^\tau$ and $s_{\rm c}/W_{\rm c}<m^\sigma$ with $\tau=\sigma=1-2^{-50}$.

quote.quote: Both exact deficits displayed above are greater than $20\cdot2^{-50}$.

children.claim: One fixed procedure transforms any bit array on $[P]\times[2^u]\times[G]\times[2^u]\times[B]$ by $(p,h,g,d,z)\mapsto(p,d,g,h,z)$ in $O(Vu^\tau)$ steps, an exact permutation even though its intermediate streams hold XOR combinations of the data.
children.method: Interchange chunks of $e=m^k$ radix-$q$ digits recursively with the bit network on rows split among its roles, then reach a general width by borrowing a few high digits of both chunks as the row field, padding rows to a multiple of $W^k$, and splitting the remaining width into base-$m$ pieces.

motivation.text: The recursion needs a power-of-$m$ width and a row field divisible by $W^k$; $O(\log e)$ high digits of the chunks themselves supply such rows at cost $O(V\log e)$, and the base-$m$ pieces cost a geometric sum dominated by the largest piece.

quote.quote: Rows for a general array can be supplied by a few of its own high digits.

children.salient: The final effect is an exact permutation, valid for arbitrary initial auxiliary values, although the procedure computes XOR combinations of data, which places it outside lower-bound models that only move data.

adds.name: chunk digit count
adds.meaning: The number of radix-$q$ digits in each chunk being interchanged.

adds.name: prime radix
adds.meaning: The fixed odd prime used as the radix of address digits, chosen to avoid every denominator of the network's matrices.

children.claim: For a fixed rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ and a fixed odd prime $q$ avoiding the denominators of its factorization, the address permutation $(H,D)\mapsto(H+AD,D)$ over $\mathbb Z/q^b\mathbb Z$, with all $H$ fields before all $D$ fields, takes exactly $a$ interchanges of $b$-digit fields and $O(V)$ further work.
children.method: Factor $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with invertible lower-triangular $E_1,E_2$, perform the triangular changes of $H$ and $D$ as controlled shifts in descending physical order, and realize each one of $\Pi$ by an add, swap, subtract sequence.

motivation.text: Controlled shifts are linear-time only when the updated field follows its controls, which lower-triangular maps respect in tape order; the factorization pushes all rank-dependent work into the partial permutation, one interchange per one.

quote.quote: Lower triangular changes of coordinates can be performed entirely in this direction.

children.claim: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ factors as $A=E_1\Pi E_2$ with $E_1,E_2$ invertible lower triangular and $\Pi$ a partial permutation matrix with exactly $a$ ones, by repeatedly eliminating around the rightmost nonzero entry of the topmost nonzero row.

quote.quote: Thus the final partial permutation matrix has exactly $a$ ones.

children.claim: A lower-triangular change of $H$ or of $D$ costs $O(V)$: updating coordinates in descending physical order, each new value is a unit multiple plus a combination of earlier coordinates, which still hold their original values.

quote.quote: A lower triangular transformation of $H$, or of $D$, costs $O(V)$: update coordinates in descending physical order.

children.claim: A one in position $(i,j)$ of $\Pi$ is done by $D_j\leftarrow D_j+H_i$, an interchange of $H_i$ and $D_j$, and $D_j\leftarrow H_i-D_j$, which takes $(h,d)$ to $(h+d,d)$ with one interchange, so the $a$ ones cost $a$ interchanges.

quote.quote: On an initial pair $(h,d)$ this sequence yields $(h+d,d)$.

children.claim: If a row field before both chunks has length divisible by $W^k$, two chunks of $e=m^k$ radix-$q$ digits can be interchanged in $O(Ve^\tau)$ time on a fixed number of tapes, preserving every other address field.
children.method: Split rows cyclically into $W$ role streams, run the bit network with frame $\Phi_{M_v}$ at each vertex, each edge being a matrix shear whose interchanges are recursive calls on $e/m$-digit fields, merge the rows back to obtain $H\gets H+D$, and finish the swap with two linear-time updates.

motivation.text: Each edge of rank $a$ costs $a$ interchanges of one $m$-th of the width on one $W$-th of the volume, and the network's ranks total $s<Wm$, so per unit of volume the recursion multiplies cost by $s/W<m^\tau$ per level while the width grows by the factor $m$.

quote.quote: Because the sum of these ranks is less than the number of wires times $m$, the resulting recurrence saves a power of the chunk width.

adds.name: recursion depth
adds.meaning: The exponent with $e=m^k$, the number of recursive levels.

adds.name: normalized cost bound
adds.meaning: A uniform bound on running time divided by logical volume for chunks of $m^k$ digits.

children.claim: Writing row $r=Wg+(w-1)$ and sending it to role $w$ as row $g$ gives $W$ streams of identical remaining shape, each of volume $V/W$ and with row count divisible by $W^{k-1}$.

quote.quote: Each has logical volume $V/W$, and its row count is divisible by $W^{k-1}$.

children.claim: With frame $\Phi_M$ at a vertex of matrix $M$, the common-frame identity and $M_{\mathrm{out}(\rho(w))}-M_{\mathrm{in}(w)}=I_m$ give output $\Phi_{I_m}f_w$ at role $\rho(w)$, so merging the rows back yields $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every original row.

quote.quote: The result is $H\leftarrow H+D$ on every original row, including rows assigned to scratch roles, whose initial values were arbitrary.

children.claim: The updates $D\leftarrow D-H$, $H\leftarrow H+D$, $D\leftarrow H-D$ send $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$, and only the middle shear uses the network.

quote.quote: The transformation sends $(H,D)$ to $(D,H)$.

children.claim: Since a node makes exactly $s$ recursive calls, each on volume $V/W$, plus $O(V)$ other work, $F_0=O(1)$ and $F_k\le(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1)$, and because $s/W<m^\tau$ this gives $F_k=O(m^{k\tau})=O(e^\tau)$.
children.method: Divide time by logical volume, so that the $W$-fold split becomes the factor $1/W$, and sum the resulting geometric series level by level.

motivation.text: Normalizing by volume makes the per-level growth factor exactly $s/W$; a naive recursion on $m$ parts would grow by $m$ per level, so the strict inequality $s/W<m^\tau<m$ is precisely what becomes the power $e^\tau$ instead of $e$.

quote.quote: After dividing cost by volume, multiplying the parameter by $m$ increases the recursive contribution by $s/W<m$.

children.claim: A depth-first schedule parks the $W-1$ inactive role streams on a stack and copies the active one, moving $O(V)$ symbols for each of the fixed number $s$ of children, so temporary storage never enters the factor $s/W$.

quote.quote: Temporary storage is therefore not substituted for logical volume in the factor $s/W$.

children.claim: Exchanging $\lceil k\log W/(2\log q)\rceil$ high digits of the two chunks and joining them gives a row field of range at least $W^k$ before both remaining chunks, which zero rows pad to a multiple of $W^k$ at most doubling the volume.

quote.quote: In the two middle orders, the first two fields form a row field of range

quote.quote: The fixed bound $a_j<m$ and the inequality $m^k<me$ make this a geometric sum of the stated order.

children.claim: Binary chunks are padded numerically from $[2^u]$ to $[q^e]$ with $e=O(u)$, which preserves the order of entries, so the bound becomes $O(Vu^\tau)$.

children.claim: For $p\ge p_0$, $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$, $r=2^{\Theta(p/d)}$ and $K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor$, one fixed procedure applies $H_0^{\otimes D}$ to bit $\rho$ of each of $D\le d$ consecutive $K$-bit chunks of an array of disk-grid polynomial records, evaluating the layer exactly and truncating once, in $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ time with error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.
children.method: Write $H_0^{\otimes D}$ as $C^{\otimes D}$ between diagonal phases; compute $C^{\otimes e}$ by running the complex network on $W$ row streams with phase frames, so that each edge is a few child layers on $e/m$ chunks between binary changes of basis done by packed selected-bit additions; borrow rows from the first chunks, solve the recurrence, and size exact Gaussian-dyadic registers for the whole layer.

motivation.text: Applying the $D$ butterflies one after another costs $D$ full passes; the complex network replaces one layer on $e$ chunks by $s<Wm$ layers on $e/m$ chunks over volume $V/W$, so the normalized cost grows like $e^\sigma$ with $\sigma<1$, provided the basis changes between them cost only $(eK)^\tau$.

quote.quote: We will obtain cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$, with $\lambda'<1$ and $V$ the logical bit volume, whereas separate butterfly factors would require $D$ whole-array passes.

children.salient: $D$ butterflies cost fewer than $D$ passes over the data, $d^{\lambda'}$ with $\lambda'<1$, and yet the result is exact up to one final truncation.

quote.quote: Also $K/\log p\to\infty$, which will make the exceptional set in a packed change of address bits small enough to repair by sorting.

children.salient: Eight modular additions flip exactly the selected parity bit and return the auxiliary chunk $z$ to its arbitrary initial value, and because the exceptional set depends only on addresses the repair bound is deterministic and worst-case.

children.claim: Each row of $H_0^{\otimes D}$ has absolute row sum one, so the exact layer maps disk arrays to disk arrays, and the single final truncation keeps the disk with error below $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$.

quote.quote: Thus $\mathcal H$ maps disk arrays to disk arrays, and componentwise truncation preserves that disk and has error less than $\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$

motivation.text: Because a pointwise product commutes with any common record permutation, the forward outputs never need to be sorted into frequency order: the opposite transform consumes exactly the order the forward transforms leave, so no full permutation is executed.

quote.quote: Pointwise multiplication commutes with applying the same record permutation $LB$ to both operands.

adds.name: polynomial ring
adds.meaning: The ring $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ of complex polynomials of degree below $r$ with $y^r=-1$.

children.method: Verify character cancellation directly in the ring, follow the recursion's branch bits to identify the stored order, invert level by level using $H_0^2=I/2$, and group the axis steps of a round.

motivation.text: In $\mathbb C[y]/(y^r+1)$ the needed roots of unity are powers of $y$, so every twiddle multiplication is an exact signed permutation of a coefficient list and only the butterflies cost arithmetic; keeping the bit-reversed output order avoids moving frequency indices.

quote.quote: Their entries will be short polynomials in a quotient where the required roots of unity act by exact signed permutations of coefficient lists.

adds.name: synthetic root
adds.meaning: The ring element $y^{2r/t}$, a primitive $t$-th root of unity that acts by a signed shift of coefficients.

adds.name: bit-reversal permutation
adds.meaning: The record permutation moving the entry at index $j$ to the bit reversal of $j$.

quote.quote: Hence the sum is zero, since the additive group of $\mathcal R_r$ has no two-torsion.

quote.quote: so the reverse procedure composed with $B_tF_t^-$ is $2^{-a}I=I/t$.

children.claim: An axis's twiddle depends only on that axis's address bits and so commutes with the other axes' butterflies, making a round a parallel butterfly $\mathcal H$ followed by multiplication by $y^E$; a contraction followed by an isometry, every round is a contraction.

quote.quote: Each $\mathcal H$ is a contraction and each $J_E$ is an isometry, so every completed round is a contraction.

quote.quote: There are at most $D(b+1)=O(dK)$ listed slots, so the moves cost $O(TpdK)$.

quote.quote: This uses at most $Dq-1$ exchanges of width-$K$ address chunks, even when the chunks are nonadjacent.

children.claim: Each round on the remaining chunks selects one common offset in $D$ consecutive chunks of a complete address set $[P]\times[2^K]^D\times[S]$, so the simultaneous layer applies at cost $O(Tpd^{\lambda'})$ per round and $O(Tp\ell d^{\lambda'})$ in total.

quote.quote: This is multiplication by $y^E$ modulo $y^r+1$.

motivation.text: Packing a polynomial into one integer turns all $r^2$ coefficient products into a single multiplication by the established $O(N\log N)$ multiplier, costing $O(rp\log(rp))$; blocks of $4p$ bits exceed twice every product coefficient, so the coefficients can be read back unambiguously.

quote.quote: Thus each resulting Gaussian integer coefficient $H_j$ is a sum of exactly $r$ signed products of Gaussian integer input coefficients of modulus at most $2^p$.

quote.quote: Four exact integer products dominate the linear packing, extraction, combination, wrapping, and truncation costs.

children.claim: The two forward errors below $\sqrt2\,\ell2^{-p}$, the product truncation and the opposite transform's error add through contractions to less than $\sqrt2(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$, which the exact scale by $M$ turns into $\sqrt2\,M(3\ell+1)2^{-p}$.
